rules.body: Apply when observer scopes share longer-lived cache state, attempts own cancellation resources, and signal consumption is lazy. README.md: "The component owns observer scope; the cache remains outside individual views." README.md: "Each actual access records consumption; each fetch owns its controller\nand completion."

For a fresh online-mode query whose last observer departs entirely offline before execution, prevent reconnect continuation from invoking its signal-consuming function with a live signal, independently of reconnect-refetch policy. TASK: "a fresh online-mode query mounted and unmounted entirely offline later calls its signal-consuming query function with a live signal after reconnect. This occurs independently of refetchOnReconnect." Check the departure-to-continuation ordering, including departure after a continuation has been queued.

Keep query-level consumption tracking distinct from attempt-owned cancellation and completion. src/workflow.py: "def consume(_):q.consumed=True;return None" README.md: "Each actual access records consumption; each fetch owns its controller\nand completion." Introducing attempt execution tracking does not itself justify moving or resetting the shared consumption record.

Preserve sharing, harmless unknown departures, cache completion for unconsumed active work, cancellation restoration, and generation isolation. README.md: "Multiple observers share one fetch. Unconsumed active work can finish into cache
after its view departs; consumed work is physically abortable. Cancellation
reverts previous query data/status and settles the originating attempt. Late
fulfillment cannot become a new attempt's data. Unknown unsubscribe is inert."

Do not generalize the fresh offline abandonment repair into cancellation of every paused or unobserved attempt. In particular, preserve entered, unconsumed work that may complete into the cache. README.md: "Unconsumed active work can finish into cache\nafter its view departs". Paused status alone does not establish whether execution has occurred or signal access has happened.

Preserve entry timing, continuation eligibility, network modes, and explicit retry scheduling. README.md: "Completion is asynchronous; initial online entry is synchronous,
paused continuation resumes on a Promise turn. First start uses network mode;
continuation also needs focus." README.md: "'always' can run offline; 'offlineFirst' allows
first offline entry but retry can pause. Retries use explicit scheduler handles."

Verify the target offline departure and reconnect sequence separately from preservation cases: one remaining observer, unknown unsubscribe, unconsumed active completion, later signal consumption, consumed-work abort and restoration, observer reuse, deferred continuation, retries, and late completion after replacement. Use TASK's live-signal failure as the target oracle and README.md's documented behavior for preservation; example outcomes do not add requirements. Keep repair scope constrained: TASK: "Preserve supported query behavior, interfaces, dependencies and build/test configuration. Change product source only."

limitations: These rules apply to the documented shared-cache and lazy-consumption mechanism; they do not establish requirements for unrelated ownership policies.
The original task does not prescribe a specific repair or choose between preventing invocation and invocation with an already-aborted signal.
The supplied code does not implement refetchOnReconnect; independence from that option is required by TASK, but its integration cannot be verified here.
The host adapter is not supplied. README.md documents its behavior, but the Python source alone cannot prove physical signal behavior or Promise timing.
The candidate's public-check results cover only the reported examples. Passing once does not establish causality, exhaustive correctness, or benefit on other tasks.

The original source does not expressly define every case involving unstarted work backed by cached data. The candidate's previous-status condition must not be promoted into a universal business requirement.
